title: Token Trace Annotator — export-first token-level cost UI and pricing patterns
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Design an 'export-first' token-level cost inspector that lets customers slice, annotate, and export cost attribution at session/message/token granularity while surfacing pricing UI patterns (slabs, tiered discounts, per-model rate-views) in the same flow. The feature should help engineers and finance owners answer: 'Which tokens and prompts are driving spend?', 'How does batching/quantization affect unit cost?', and 'What billing artifacts do we provide for chargeback?'

Scope: interactive explorer panel within Console -> Usage -> Cost Insights; a lightweight step-through export wizard (CSV, JSON, attachment-ready); UI recipes for showing price bands and applied discounts; inline preview of exported rows and PII scrub controls. The design must consider performance of rendering many token rows, trust boundaries for PII in exports, and key pricing tradeoffs (human-readable vs system-precise data).
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype for explorer + export wizard completed and approved by PM
Usability test with 6 internal engineers and 4 finance stakeholders, task success >= 80%
Design tokens and visual spec (colors/typography/spacing) included in handoff document
Accessibility checklist passed (contrast, keyboard nav, screen reader labels)
Handoff includes sample export schema and explicit PII masking options and API mapping
tasks: Draft initial exploration patterns (heat rows, token sparklines, attribution chip)
Create step-through export wizard flows (selection, preview, scrub, download)
Align on pricing pattern visuals with PM: slab vs dynamic vs hybrid
Prototype data pivots: per-session, per-message, per-token-range
Internal review with Eng to validate performance constraints & limits
Security review on export artifacts (PII, retention, KMS notes)
Finalize handoff artifacts and create GitHub issue for engineering implementation
decisions: Export-first model chosen to reduce cognitive load: users will be guided to export a representative sample before requesting full-run exports
Default export granularity set to 'message-level with token ranges'; advanced option exposes full per-token rows
PII is never exported by default. Export wizard requires explicit toggles for 'include user content' with audit log recording
Pricing UI will show two perspectives: 'Display price' (rounded, human-facing) and 'Billing price' (raw tokens x precise rate) toggled in preview
To improve performance, token sparklines are aggregated client-side and lazy-loaded; full token table is paginated server-side with a 10k-row limit per export request
review_comments: PM (Anika Rao): Please ensure the export schema maps to Billing's canonical fields (billing_line_item_id, model_version_tag, effective_rate). Add example rows in the PRD.
Eng (Diego Morales): We need an API contract for sampling exports vs bulk job export. Concerned about synchronous generation; propose background job with status URL.
Security (Priya Nambiar): Flagging PII — require tenant-level policy and opt-in with KMS envelope for exported payloads. Mark security_review_required true.
Design (Jules Park): Consider micro-interactions for price-band hover states to explain discount application; add tooltips for quantization/approx charge adjustments.
Customer Success (Marco Liu): Add recommended export presets for common chargeback customers (team-monthly, app-feature, prompt-campaign).
